claim: Players rotate Tetris zoids physically more than a plan-first model predicts, to expose shape and fit sooner; physical rotation (about 100 ms plus ~200 ms key choice) is much faster than mental rotation (800-1800 ms).
agent_test: Same-lab, same-game evidence only. Test: agent with a cheap tool probe vs the same agent forced to reason internally, equal tokens, on tasks where a probe is cheap.

claim: Extra (epistemic) rotations rise with skill (7% expert, 4% beginner episodes; N=2 players) and shorten time to final orientation (676 vs 1127 ms; 754 vs 1122 ms).
agent_test: Gap search: the only large-sample test (Destefano, Lindstedt and Gray 2011, N=59, 173 games) finds the opposite or a hump (d18), so the 'rises with skill' side rests on two players. Weight now favours 'falls or peaks then falls'. Test: probe rate vs task familiarity in the agent; expect a hump.

claim: In a controlled lab task, a preview (an external action that shows the shape) raises accuracy (.86 vs .53) and speeds responses (869 vs 1791 ms); benefit-cost ratio exceeds 1 and rises with lag.
agent_test: All from one lab (Maglio, Wenger); no independent replication found (d03, d33). The odd t values and df are printed in the original paper (d01), not a copying error: do not cite them. Test: forced-probe vs no-probe arms on a hidden-state toy task at equal tokens.

claim: Hands/pointing reduce time and errors in coin counting (22.5 vs 18.7 s; 68% vs 42% errors, N=5).
agent_test: Tiny N, one text with a p-value typo. Weak support; do not rely on it.

claim: Executing code or tools to get grounded feedback improves LLM agents over reasoning alone (ReAct ALFWorld best 71% vs Act 45%; InterCode-SQL Try Again GPT-4 9.1 to 73.7; CRITIC with tool beats without).
agent_test: Gains shrink for strong models and depend on tool quality. Test: probe-first vs attempt-first at equal tokens on code tasks.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external signal does not help and can hurt (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 for GPT-4); oracle or tool feedback helps.
agent_test: Test: critique round with vs without an executed check, equal tokens.

claim: Self-repair is not a free win at equal compute: GPT-4 repair budget grids give about 1.05x and 0.97x of the pass rate for equal-sample budgets; quality of feedback is the bottleneck (33.30% own vs 52.60% human feedback).
agent_test: Chen et al. report bigger gains (+12% TransCoder) and LDB reports gains that keep rising; budget accounting differs. Test: probe tokens vs extra samples.

claim: Verifier-style tests (reproduction and regression tests) lift issue resolution at low cost: Agentless majority vote 25.67% to 32.0% with reproduction tests, $0.70 per issue; SWT-Bench test-before-submit raised test success 15.9 to 18.5%.
agent_test: Selection benefit is separable from probing benefit. Test: tests used for selection vs tests used to steer the next attempt.

claim: LLMs are weak at choosing which question or probe to ask: QuestBench Logic-Q and Planning-Q under 50% (vs over 80% on GSM-Q); accuracy falls with search depth.
agent_test: One benchmark in four entries. Test: ask-vs-act decision accuracy in the agent.

claim: Explicit expected-information-gain selection of questions or probes beats prompting alone (UoT +38.1% average; BED-LLM +37.4 points; EIG-uniform best rank in 20 Questions).
agent_test: Gaps shrink with stronger models (b21); some domains are closed-set games. Test: EIG-scored probe choice vs free choice at equal tokens.

claim: Missing information is costly: multi-turn underspecified input drops performance by 39% on average, and asking clarification helps (clarification F1 +73% on ALFWorld-Clarification).
agent_test: Clarification differs from probing the world. Test: when the answer is in the world, probe; when with the user, ask.

claim: LLMs explore badly in context: GPT-4 basic prompt shows suffix failure in over 60% of replicates; only one configuration worked.
agent_test: One paper, four entries. Test: scripted probe budgets vs free exploration.

claim: Tool overuse is a real boundary: base models call tools unnecessarily over 30% of the time; a calibrated agent cut tool use 24% and raised performance 37.1%. Under-use also occurs: some agents call a simulator in under 1% of cases (d20), and a planner-less agent asks about twice the planner optimum (d26).
schema_part: S4 (probe only when value exceeds cost)
agent_test: Test: add a probe-cost check (value of information vs cost) and measure unneeded and missed probes.

claim: Humans and LLMs differ in active information gathering: conjunctive rules are harder for all, humans needed 9.6 vs 6.4 tests; gpt-5 and deepseek-reasoner near-perfect on disjunctive rules.
agent_test: Samiei and BoxingGym differ in task; BoxingGym finds model-fitting does not reliably help. Test: structured hypothesis-test loop vs free probing.

claim: Agentic test-time scaling with execution helps: Claude-4.5-Opus 70.9 to 77.6 on SWE-Bench Verified; repeated-sampling coverage grows log-linearly (15.9% to 56%).
agent_test: Sampling gains need a verifier; plateau beyond hundreds of samples. Test: split budget between probes and samples.

claim: No study tests Kirsh and Maglio's epistemic-action hypothesis by name as a probe-before-attempt test on an LLM. Named-term items found: a position paper with no data (c01), a belief-query study that cites Kirsh and Maglio (d19, figures only), an ASK-action study with o3-mini (d26), and a Tetris serving benchmark (c21).
agent_test: Absence claim from search limits. Test: build the named experiment (U1).

claim: Passing a probe result forward to the next attempt (not only using it to rerank) raises repair success: a generated reproduction test as input gave a plausible fix on 17 of 23 bugs vs 13 of 23, and 33% vs 2% per run when used. Test was oracle-filtered, so this is an upper bound.
agent_test: Gap 2. Only one steering study, 23 bugs, oracle-filtered tests. Test: arm A probe output fed to attempt 2; arm B probe used only to choose among k attempts; equal tokens.

claim: A probe the model writes itself can mislead: patches passing the agent's own reproducer failed the real tests in 17-30% of cases for open-process agents (4-5% for a fixed workflow), reproducers trigger the bug only 41-57% of the time, and models copy a silently wrong tool output (accuracy up to 47% below the no-tool best).
agent_test: Gap 10. 2024-era models. A one-line warning that tools can be wrong gave up to +30% (d25). Test: misleading vs neutral toy case; measure right-to-wrong flips; add a rule that the probe must fail on the broken case first.

claim: In a large Tetris sample (59 players, 173 games, scores to over 1 million) complementary actions fall with expertise: lenient rules give a hump, stricter rules near zero, and no player above 100,000 points used strict translation actions in more than 2% of episodes.
agent_test: Gap 6. Rules are log-based and confound goal switching; conference paper. Test: probe rate against how often the task type has appeared in the session.

claim: Having a probe tool is not a probe policy: agents both under-use (a simulator called in under 1% of cases, 15% of rollouts misused, up to 5% worse when enforced) and over-use (over 30% unnecessary calls; ASK actions about twice the planner optimum) outside-information tools.
agent_test: Gap 3. Different tools (simulator, search, ASK). No tested value-of-information gate for code probes. Test: fixed rule vs confidence gate vs EIG-style score (U2, U4).

claim: Gating an expensive step on a failed outside check beats always doing it: try-first-then-plan lifted Pass@1 (Qwen3-4B 76.05 to 83.13) at 4.85 cost units vs 8.31 for plan-first, because 76% of problems are solved directly.
agent_test: Gap 3. The gated step is planning, not probing; easy benchmarks. Test: same gate on the probe step (U2).

claim: Probe output costs context, and trimming it is free: masking tool outputs older than 10 turns cut cost by over half with no loss in solve rate (Qwen3-Coder 480B: 52% cheaper, +2.6 points); model summaries lengthened runs by hiding failure signals.
agent_test: Gap 9. One scaffold, software tasks. Test: keep probe conclusion only vs full output vs summary; accuracy and tokens.

claim: Whether probing helps less as models get stronger is unresolved: code actions gained more for stronger models (up to +20% absolute, gains widen with ability), while belief queries gave only small gains to a model that already saturates easy tasks and large gains on a task it had not saturated.
agent_test: Gap 4. Different probe kinds and tasks. Hard tasks fail more for every agent (66-73% easy vs 4.8-19% hard, d21). Test: run U1 by difficulty bin on 2-3 model sizes (U6, U11).

claim: At matched budget, more interaction steps beat longer thinking per step for a small prompted web agent (23.81 baseline; check-again 26.14, budget forcing 24.81, best-of-n 25.03), but prompted re-checks can flip right answers to wrong.
agent_test: Gap 1. 1-3 point gaps, 3 runs, one 12B model; re-check is not a world probe. No matched-budget probe-first vs attempt-first study found (d34). Test: U1.

claim: Code is an effective probe medium: executable code actions gave up to 20% higher success and up to 30% fewer actions than JSON or text actions, with higher success for 12 of 17 models.
agent_test: Gap 7. Tests the action format, not which probe kind pays most; no study ranks run-code vs print-state vs tiny-test vs ask-user. Test: probe-kind arms on the same items.
